papers.title: Using Transformers to Generate 3-Manifold Triangulations
papers.abstract: Using dehydration signatures as an encoding, we train GPT-2-style transformers to generate triangulations of 3-dimensional manifolds. Our main runs each use approximately 3 exaFLOPs, spanning a 200 million parameter model trained on 60 million sphere triangulations to an 11 million parameter model trained on 1.1 billion sphere triangulations. The optimal model has 10 blocks, width 640 and generates dehydration signatures of closed manifolds of various topological types at a rate of 6.9%, 82% of which are spheres. To investigate how our method scales, we use the technique of IsoFLOP curves on 15-tetrahedron triangulations of the 3-sphere, over a compute range of 6 to 3000 petaFLOPs, and observe neural scaling behaviour. We extract a parameter scaling exponent of $\alpha = 0.49$ ($[0.48, 0.50]$ stat, $\pm 0.02$ syst), and an optimal ratio of 234 tokens per parameter for training. In addition, we present a number of smaller experiments, including evidence that transformers are able to learn to count degree-one edges near-perfectly, but get progressively worse when counting edges with higher degrees.

papers.title: The residual map as a stratified fibration over the resonance arrangement
papers.abstract: Given a stratum $\mathcal{H}(\mu)$ of meromorphic one-forms on a Riemann surface with prescribed orders of zeros and poles, the residual map assigns to each differential the collection of its residues at the poles. In this paper, we prove that the residual map is a locally trivial topological fibration over each open flat of the stratification induced by the resonance arrangement. To give an algebro-geometric proof of this result, we introduce a refined compactification of the projectivized stratum $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{H}(\mu)$, namely the moduli space of residue-aligned multi-scale differentials $\operatorname{RAMS}(\mu)$. We prove that the projectivized residual map extends to $\operatorname{RAMS}(\mu)$ as a stratified fibration over the projectivized resonance arrangement, thereby yielding a resolution of the projectivized residual map. This approach naturally extends to the analogue of the residual map for strata of $k$-differentials. Complementing the algebro-geometric approach, we also develop a flat-geometric point of view. In genus zero, each isoresidual fiber carries a canonical higher-dimensional analogue of a translation structure. These fibers admit a metric completion whose boundary has a modular interpretation in terms of the WYSIWYG compactification, for which we provide explicit local models. Isoresidual fibers admit a polyhedral cell decomposition whose geometry varies linearly with the underlying configuration of residues in period coordinates. Degenerations of these cells occur precisely when resonance conditions are satisfied, providing a geometric proof that the residual map is a stratified fibration. Finally, certain isoresidual fibers admit natural interpretations as Hurwitz spaces of branched covers, yielding unexpected homeomorphisms between moduli spaces of covers with prescribed ramification profiles.

papers.title: Profinite Non-Rigidity of Arithmetic Lattices and the K\"ahler Property
papers.abstract: We study the profinite non-rigidity of arithmetic lattices and its implications for the K\"ahler property. In the first part, we characterize the absolute Dynkin types that admit non-isomorphic real forms of higher-rank Lie groups containing torsion-free arithmetic lattices with isomorphic profinite completions. In the second part, as a geometric application, we answer a question asked independently by Arapura and Libgober, by showing that the K\"ahlerness of finitely presented, residually finite groups is not determined by its profinite completion.

papers.title: Measures of maximal entropy for monotone factors of smooth surface diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We prove that a transitive monotone factor of a smooth surface diffeomorphism has a unique measure of maximal entropy whenever its topological entropy is positive. Its entropy is the entropy of a single homoclinic class of the diffeomorphism, and the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on every ergodic measure with positive entropy of that class. The other homoclinic classes are mapped to periodic orbits. We give an application to the essential factor of a diffeomorphism isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov map ---possibly relative to a finite invariant set--- constructed by Garc\'ia-Sassi \& Tal: the essential factor has a unique measure of maximal entropy, which is Bernoulli and has full support.

papers.title: Topological classification of Bazaikin spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a topological classification of Bazaikin spaces whose sixth cohomology groups have orders prime to \(5\). Moreover, we obtain an estimate for the number of diffeomorphism types among these spaces.

papers.title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
papers.abstract: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.

papers.title: Braided Multisections and Akhmedov's Fake Quadrics
papers.abstract: We give handlebody decompositions of the complements of the cyclic multisections in $\Sigma_g\times S^2$ constructed in~\cite{AB}. The 2-handle framings are induced by the product coordinates. We compute the integral homology of the complements from their handle chain complexes, including the torsion subgroup of $H_2$. For the degree pairs $(3,3)$ and $(2,4)$, we specify surface diffeomorphisms inducing the maps on first homology prescribed in~\cite{AY} and recover the integral first homology groups $(\Z/3)^2\oplus\Z/(3m)$ and $(\Z/2)^2\oplus\Z/(4m)$, respectively, for $m\geq1$. For the symmetric $m=1$ sum, we also give a simultaneous surface diagram of the relative product attachments and identify their product framings with the surface framings. The resulting symplectic sums are aspherical and symplectically minimal, and have the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$.

papers.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
papers.abstract: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.

papers.title: Counting multigeodesics and the Selberg-Delange method
papers.abstract: We study the counting function $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$ for $m$-multigeodesics of length at most $x$ on a compact hyperbolic surface $X$ where $m$ is a positive integer. Building on the Selberg-Delange method, originally developed for counting integers with exactly $m$ prime factors in the interval $[1,x]$, we prove a large $x$ asymptotic for $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$. We show that for fixed $m$ as $x\to\infty$ the asymptotic is independent of the surface, whereas for $\frac{m}{\log x}$ bounded away from zero, the asymptotic depends on an infinite Euler product over the lengths of primitive closed geodesics. We also study the distribution of the function $\omega_1$, defined on multigeodesics $\Gamma$ as $\omega_1(\Gamma)=k-1$ for $\Gamma=(\gamma_1,...,\gamma_k)$ a $k$-multigeodesic. We show that as $x\to\infty$, the distribution of $\omega_1$ in the set of multigeodesics of length $\leq x$ is close to that of a Poisson random variable with parameter $\log x$. Both of these theorems rely on studying the generating function of the random variable $\omega_1$ which we relate to the Selberg zeta function.

papers.title: Worldsheet skeins and block decomposition of quivers
papers.abstract: Following the knot-quiver correspondence, we investigate quiver counterparts of the HOMFLYPT skein relations by interpreting link invariants in terms of holomorphic worldsheets and their multicover contributions. Extending this framework to more general worldsheet geometries, we conjecture that, up to quiver equivalence, the adjacency matrix of the quiver associated with any link in a skein triple admits a block decomposition whose diagonal blocks are quiver adjacency matrices associated with the other two links. We verify this conjecture in numerous examples.

papers.title: Quantifying discontinuity
papers.abstract: Given a compact space $X$ that does not admit an embedding (an injective continuous function) into $\mathbb{R}^d$, we study the discontinuity that any injective function $X \to \mathbb{R}^d$ must have. To this end, we define a scale invariant modulus of discontinuity and obtain general lower bounds, thus obtaining quantified nonembeddability results of Haefliger--Weber type. Moreover, we establish analogous lower bounds for simplicial complexes that do not admit an almost $r$-embedding in $\mathbb{R}^d$, thus obtaining a quantified version of the topological Tverberg theorem.

papers.title: Ropelength-Filtered Reidemeister Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove relative smoothing with uniform reach control for one-parameter families of positive-reach $C^{1,1}$ knots and combine it with relative multijet transversality to obtain projection-generic regularization inside strict ropelength sublevels. Passing to a lifted Reidemeister multigraph reconstructs the admissible $\pi_0$ of every strict projection-framed ropelength sublevel, and the right-relaxed diagrammatic merge scale equals the geometric one. The normalised projection-framed sublevels are compact, so connected merge levels are attained. These degree-zero results are organized by a fibre cosheaf: a filtered relational cellular cosheaf of sets on the planar Reidemeister multigraph, whose stalks are strict fibre components and whose costalks are the relations realized by Reidemeister movies. The lifted multigraph is its Grothendieck construction, reconstruction is a descent statement, and the diagram image is its support. The diagram image computes merges exactly when no stalk is persistently separated, and a canonical flat coarsening is the coarsest diagram-indexed model that computes components. For amphichiral knots the spherical diagram image cannot detect mirror barriers, whereas the planar image can; no planar type of the standard diagrams of $4_1$ and $6_3$ is fixed by crossing switch. Symmetric hubs and finite certificates give upper bounds for mirror merges, and sign separators give lower bounds. For finite recognition we distinguish full rooted-ball occurrence, visibility in the monotone diagram-image filtration, and saturation. Every finite Reidemeister submultigraph becomes visible at a finite ropelength level, a visible saturated Barbensi-Celoria characteristic certificate determines the knot type up to mirroring, and a universal computable crossing-complexity bound controls visibility.
